# AART

> A package manager for agent artifacts. It installs skills, guidelines, MCP servers, hooks and
> memory into agentic harnesses, from a Registry somebody in your organization reviewed. The
> executable and the package are `aart-cli`; the Python import package is `aart_cli`.

The command reference is not written down here. Run `aart-cli docs --json` for every command with
its description, usage, options, defaults and choices, read from the installed version when it
runs. Every mutation reviews first and changes nothing until it is run again with `--yes`; `--json`
changes only the output.

## Guides

- [README](README.md): installing AART and the shortest route to an installed artifact
- [Using an installed AART](docs/using/consumer-lifecycle-v1.md): install, update, check and undo
- [Maintaining a registry](docs/registry/maintaining-a-registry-v1.md): from an Upstream repository to an approved artifact
- [Writing an artifact](docs/authoring/authoring-an-artifact-v1.md): the manifest and its check
- [Rolling out on GitHub Enterprise Server](docs/ci/github-enterprise-rollout.md): what changes on an Enterprise instance and in a fork

## Optional

- [Product Specification](docs/product-specification/PRODUCT_SPECIFICATION.md): the single source of product truth; long, and it describes the target as well as what is shipped
